c.request: Applying a 4.99 cutoff on the payment amount, take the qualifying payments that can be linked to a rental and, through that rental, to an inventory item (leave out payments without such a match). For each rental and store (`inventory.store_id`), total the payment amounts and count the payments. Then for each store, show the store id, the average of those per-rental totals, and the average number of payments per rental (both unrounded, ignoring missing values). Only payments larger than 4.99 are included. Payments of exactly 4.99 are left out.
c.sql:
WITH rental_payments AS (
  SELECT 
    r.rental_id,
    i.store_id,
    SUM(p.amount) AS rental_total,
    COUNT(*) AS payment_count
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
  WHERE p.amount > 4.99
  GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id
)
SELECT 
  store_id,
  AVG(rental_total) AS avg_per_rental_total,
  AVG(payment_count) AS avg_payments_per_rental
FROM rental_payments
GROUP BY store_id
ORDER BY store_id

d.request: For each store, calculate the average payment amount per rental and average payment count per rental, using only payments with amount strictly greater than 4.99 that match to exactly one rental and inventory item.
d.sql: SELECT store_id, AVG(payment_avg) as avg_payment_amount, AVG(payment_count) as avg_payment_count_per_rental FROM (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, AVG(p.amount) as payment_avg, COUNT(p.payment_id) as payment_count FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id WHERE p.amount > 4.99 GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id) t GROUP BY store_id

a.request: Take the payments of more than 4.99 that can be linked to a rental and, through that rental, to an inventory item (leave out payments without such a match). For each rental and store (`inventory.store_id`), total the payment amounts and count the payments. Then for each store, show the store id, the average of those per-rental totals, and the average number of payments per rental (both unrounded, ignoring missing values).
a.sql:
WITH rental_payments AS (
  SELECT 
    r.rental_id,
    i.store_id,
    p.amount
  FROM payment p
  INNER JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
  INNER JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
  WHERE p.amount > 4.99
),
rental_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    rental_id,
    store_id,
    SUM(amount) AS total_amount,
    COUNT(*) AS payment_count
  FROM rental_payments
  GROUP BY rental_id, store_id
)
SELECT 
  store_id,
  AVG(total_amount) AS avg_total_per_rental,
  AVG(payment_count) AS avg_payment_count_per_rental
FROM rental_totals
GROUP BY store_id
ORDER BY store_id

b.request: Payments with amount strictly greater than 4.99 linked to rentals with inventory, grouped by rental and store to sum payment amounts and count payments, then for each store report store ID, the average of per-rental payment sums, and the average of per-rental payment counts.
b.sql: SELECT rental_totals.store_id, AVG(rental_totals.total_amount) AS avg_payment_sum_per_rental, AVG(rental_totals.payment_count) AS avg_payment_count_per_rental FROM (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(p.payment_id) AS payment_count FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id WHERE p.amount > 4.99 GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id) AS rental_totals GROUP BY rental_totals.store_id ORDER BY rental_totals.store_id
